new_task_1.title: Improve Docker runner handling for layout roots and isolated profile caches
new_task_1.description: The Docker runner now handles consumers launched from subfolders that declare a higher-level `layout().folders.root`, and isolated `clean` or `copy` cache modes copy the actual requested profiles, including the implicit default build profile when needed. The runner also accepts an optional Docker build platform setting from runner configuration when building the image.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure Docker runner executions keep working for recipes located under a declared layout root and for isolated cache modes that rely on host/build profiles, while allowing runner configuration to forward an optional Docker image build platform.

expectation.grounded: When a Docker runner command is invoked for a consumer whose `layout()` defines `folders.root` above the current recipe folder, the runner should mount that root folder into the container and rewrite the in-container working path so Conan still sees the correct project-relative layout and root-level files. When runner cache mode is `clean` or `copy`, the runner should copy the explicitly requested host and build profiles into `.conanrunner/profiles`, and if no build profile was provided it should also copy the default build profile so container-side Conan can resolve build context settings. If the runner configuration provides a Docker build platform, that value should be forwarded to the Docker image build step.
expectation.conceptual: Containerized Conan runs should behave like local runs even when the recipe lives in a subdirectory of a larger layout-rooted project, and isolated runner caches should not fail just because the container does not automatically have the right profiles. Users should also be able to request a specific Docker build platform through runner configuration.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the shared-cache runner mode beyond leaving the host cache mounted as before. Continue requiring either a Dockerfile or image name. Preserve existing runner cache semantics apart from copying only the profiles actually needed for the invocation and the implicit default build profile when Conan would otherwise rely on it.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should expand compatibility for existing Docker runner workflows without changing the overall command model or forcing users to restructure their projects.

behavior: Docker runner commands can now operate from recipe subfolders whose layout root is defined higher in the project tree.
In isolated `clean` and `copy` cache modes, the runner now stages the requested profiles into the container workspace instead of assuming the whole profile set is already available there.
When no build profile is explicitly passed, the runner copies Conan's default build profile so container-side profile resolution still succeeds.
Runner configuration can now provide a Docker build platform that is forwarded during image build.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe in a subfolder defines `layout().folders.root` pointing to a parent folder and is executed through the Docker runner, the containerized Conan command should still succeed using the correct root-relative project files.

When the Docker runner uses `cache=clean` or `cache=copy` and the invocation relies on Conan's implicit default build profile, the container setup should copy that default build profile and complete successfully instead of failing due to a missing profile.
When explicit host and build profiles are provided to an isolated Docker runner invocation, those profiles should be copied into the runner workspace used inside the container.
When runner configuration specifies a Docker build platform, the Docker image build step should use that platform value.

new_task_2.title: Add deprecated legacy multi-remote update policy
new_task_2.description: Conan 2.13.0 adds a built-in `core:update_policy=legacy` compatibility mode for recipe update checks across multiple remotes. When enabled for `--update` or explicit update checks, Conan restores the older remote-order behavior that only considers the first remote where each revision appears, and it emits a deprecation warning for that mode.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure users who depend on the previous multi-remote update resolution behavior can opt back into it explicitly, while making the compatibility mode visible as deprecated.

expectation.grounded: Conan should recognize `core:update_policy=legacy` as a built-in configuration value. When recipe resolution is running with update semantics (`--update` or check-update) and that conf is set, Conan should query recipe revisions from each remote, keep only the first occurrence of each distinct revision in remote order, and then choose the newest timestamp among those filtered revisions. It should emit a deprecation warning the first time this legacy policy is used. When the conf is not set, Conan should keep using the standard update behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users with workflows that relied on the old remote-order update policy should be able to preserve that behavior deliberately during migration, but Conan should signal that the mode is temporary and slated for removal.

constraints.grounded: Apply this legacy policy only when update behavior is requested; normal non-update resolution should continue using the existing lookup path. Limit the compatibility mode to recipe revision selection across remotes and do not suppress the deprecation warning when the mode is used.
constraints.conceptual: The new setting should act as an explicit compatibility escape hatch, not replace the current default behavior.

behavior: A new built-in conf key `core:update_policy` accepts the value `legacy`.
With `core:update_policy=legacy` and update semantics enabled, Conan restores remote-order first-occurrence filtering before comparing revision timestamps across remotes.
Using the legacy policy emits a deprecation warning indicating that the mode will be removed in a future version.
Without the legacy conf, multi-remote update resolution continues using the normal 2.13.0 behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe update check runs across multiple remotes without `core:update_policy=legacy`, Conan should keep selecting revisions according to the standard 2.13.0 update behavior.

When the same update check runs with `core:update_policy=legacy`, Conan should select among revisions using the first remote occurrence of each revision before timestamp ordering, reproducing the older remote-order behavior.
When `core:update_policy=legacy` is used, Conan should emit a deprecation warning to user-facing output.
When update behavior is not requested, enabling `core:update_policy=legacy` should not change ordinary recipe lookup behavior.

new_task_3.title: Emit CPS packages in a CMake-discoverable layout with prefix metadata
new_task_3.description: The CPS generator now writes generated `.cps` files under a `cps/` subdirectory inside the configuration-specific output folder, and the serialized CPS metadata moves to spec version `0.13.0` with a `prefix` entry derived from the package folder.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure generated CPS dependency metadata matches newer CPS/CMake discovery expectations for both file location and serialized package prefix information.

expectation.grounded: When `CPSDeps` generates metadata for a dependency configuration, it should place the `.cps` files under `build/cps/<config>/cps/` instead of directly under `build/cps/<config>/`. The serialized CPS document should report `cps_version` as `0.13.0` and include `prefix` set to the dependency package folder normalized with forward slashes. Deserialization should preserve the new prefix field when loading CPS data.
expectation.conceptual: CPS consumers should find generated packages in the layout CMake expects and should receive an explicit install prefix in the CPS metadata so downstream tools know where the package content lives.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing CPS package content such as name, version, configurations, and supplemental metadata intact aside from the updated CPS version and added prefix field. Only change the output location to the extra `cps/` directory rather than redesigning the rest of the generator structure.
constraints.conceptual: The update should improve compatibility with CPS tooling without changing the meaning of the dependency metadata already being emitted.

behavior: Generated `.cps` files now live in a `cps/` subdirectory beneath the configuration-specific CPS output folder.
Serialized CPS documents now include a `prefix` field pointing at the dependency package folder.
Loading CPS data round-trips the new `prefix` field.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer runs `CPSDeps`, the generated package metadata file for a configuration should be written under `build/cps/<config>/cps/<name>.cps`.
When inspecting a generated CPS file, its JSON should include `cps_version` equal to `0.13.0`.
When inspecting that generated CPS file, its JSON should include `prefix` set to the dependency package folder path using forward slashes.
When CPS metadata is deserialized and re-serialized, the `prefix` value should be preserved.

new_task_4.title: Handle dotted package names correctly in generated CMake examples
new_task_4.description: The `conan new` CMake template rendering now preserves dots in package-oriented names where generated files and includes need them, while still normalizing dots to underscores for generated C++ symbol references. This fixes scaffolded examples for package names such as `mydep.pkg.team`.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure `conan new` CMake templates generate compilable example code for packages and requirements whose names contain dots, without breaking identifier-oriented template substitutions that still need sanitized names.

expectation.grounded: When `NewAPI` derives template names from a reference, helper values intended to represent package names should no longer strip `.` by default, so dotted names can remain intact in rendered package-oriented strings such as include-facing names. At the same time, identifier-oriented substitutions such as `package_name` should continue to normalize `.` to `_`, and generated C++ call sites in the `cmake_lib` template should explicitly replace `.` with `_` when referencing dependency function symbols.
expectation.conceptual: Generated projects should preserve dotted package identity where filenames or include names rely on it, but the C++ symbols inside those generated files should still be valid identifiers.

constraints.grounded: Continue normalizing `-` and `+` to `_` for generated identifier helpers. Keep the existing version-stripping behavior for reference-derived names. Limit the symbol-specific dot normalization to the identifier contexts that require valid C++ names.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should make dotted package names work in generated examples without changing naming behavior for unrelated template inputs.

behavior: Reference-derived template names no longer remove dots indiscriminately.
Identifier-oriented template values still normalize dots to underscores where generated code requires valid identifiers.
The generated `cmake_lib` source template now converts dotted requirement names to underscore-separated function-call symbols.
Scaffolded examples for dotted package names can build without manual renaming of generated includes or symbols.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan new cmake_lib` for a package whose name contains dots, the generated template should preserve the dotted package-oriented name where the scaffold expects that package identity.

When the generated example code references dependency function symbols derived from dotted requirement names, those symbol references should use underscore-normalized identifiers so the C++ code is valid.
When building a scaffolded project that uses dotted package names in generated references, the project should no longer require manual edits just to reconcile dotted names with generated C++ symbols.
When package names contain `-` or `+`, the existing underscore normalization behavior for identifier-oriented template values should remain in place.
